faqs.q: Sec. 14-203. - Notice of impoundment and payment.
faqs.a:
(a)
Notice of impoundment and payment.
As soon as is practicable after impoundment of an animal, an animal management officer
               will give the owner notice of impoundment and payment, if the owner is known. The
               notification may be given by any method reasonably calculated to reach the owner promptly,
               including but not limited to delivering the notice in-person, by posting at the owner's
               last known address, or by electronic mail or text message. If the owner is not known
               to the animal management officer, the animal management officer or designee thereof
               will make reasonable efforts to determine the owner and give notice of the impoundment.
Exception.
An animal management officer is not obligated to determine the owner of any cat deemed
               in the sole discretion of the officer to be feral. A feral cat may be impounded, transported
               to the shelter, and may be disposed of in accordance with
section 14-205
of this article.
(1)
Contents of notice.
The notice of impoundment and payment must contain the following:
(i)
A notice that an animal has been impounded and the location to which the animal has
                  or will be transported;
(ii)
The process by which the owner or custodian may redeem or prevent disposition of the
                  animal;
(iii)
The amounts determined by the animal management officer to be sufficient to reimburse
                  the city for the costs related to the impoundment, and by the shelter sufficient to
                  provide for the animal's care and provision for at least 30 days including the day
                  on which the animal was impounded; and
(iv)
A notice that an impounded animal not redeemed as set forth herein will be considered
                  abandoned and disposed of.
(
Ord. No. 4878
, § 9, 10-7-2024)
